title: Bank Deposit Sending Limits and the Per-Recipient Frequency Cap
content:
A Bank Deposit transfer is booked only under the customer's own Personal Sender Account, and only while that account's status is active. Its principal must then fit every ceiling that applies at the moment of booking.

## Clauses

**1. Account.** A Bank Deposit transfer is booked only under the customer's own Personal Sender Account, and only while that account's status is active. This is read from the account record held by Paloma, not from the customer's statement.

**2. Account-level ceilings.** The principal must fit every sending ceiling of the account's level at the moment of booking, aggregated over all of the customer's personal transfers in Bank Deposit, Cash Pickup and Mobile Wallet: the principal sent in the last 24 hours, in the last 30 days and in the last 180 days, the number of transfers in the last 24 hours, and the number of corridors used in the last 30 days.

**3. Tier range.** The principal must lie between the tier's smallest and largest principal, both inclusive.

**4. Real-time corridor ceiling.** On a tier whose payout rail is local real time, the principal may not exceed the corridor's real-time ceiling; a corridor with no listed ceiling has no ceiling below the tier's largest principal.

**5. Per-recipient frequency.** No more than the tier's per-recipient figure of Bank Deposit transfers to one recipient may be booked, counted including the new one. The count takes Bank Deposit transfers to the same saved recipient booked strictly later than 24 hours before the moment of handling, leaving out transfers whose status is cancelled or refunded. The count is read from the transfer records.

**6. Binding ceiling.** The binding ceiling for one transfer is the lowest of the account level's per-transfer limit, the tier's largest principal and the corridor ceiling.

**7. Over a ceiling.** A booking over any ceiling is not made. The customer may lower the principal, pick a tier or delivery method whose ceiling fits, wait for the window, or raise the account level. Paloma never splits one requested amount into several transfers.

## Per-recipient count: boundary cases (hypothetical times)

Tier allowing 3 transfers to one recipient; handling at 12:00 on a given day.

| Earlier transfers to this recipient | Counted? |
|---|---|
| Booked 12:00 the previous day (exactly 24 hours earlier) | no; not strictly later than 24 hours before |
| Booked 12:01 the previous day | yes |
| Booked 09:00 today, now cancelled | no; cancelled transfers are left out |
| Booked 10:00 today, deposited | yes |

With two counted transfers, the new booking makes three, which is within a figure of 3; with three counted transfers the new booking would make four and is not made.

## Binding ceiling: worked example (hypothetical figures)

On Bank Deposit Express to Ghana (GH-GHS), with an account-level per-transfer limit of 2500.00: the tier's largest principal is 2999.00 and the corridor ceiling is 1900.00, so the binding ceiling is the lowest of the three, 1900.00. A request for 2000.00 is not booked and is not split; the customer may lower it to 1900.00 or less, or choose a tier or delivery method whose ceiling fits.
